item.title: Panic on Denver Airport runway: American Airlines aborts takeoff after gear malfunction; video shows passengers fleeing down slides as smoke engulfs plane
item.description: An American Airlines flight bound for Miami aborted takeoff at Denver International Airport due to a landing gear malfunction. Dramatic footage showed passengers evacuating via emergency slides as smoke and flames erupted from the aircraft's rear. The airline identified a tyre issue on the Boeing 737 MAX 8.

item.title: ‘Totally illegal’: Trump accuses Democrats of fraud for paying millions for celebrity endorsements; demands prosecution against Kamala Harris
item.description: Donald Trump has accused the Democratic Party of illegal activities during the 2024 presidential campaign. He alleged that the Democrats funneled millions to celebrities like Beyoncé, Oprah Winfrey, and Al Sharpton for endorsements. Trump claims these payments are illegal and were incorrectly documented.

item.title: 'Declare meats, fruits, vegetables': Travelers to US get weird reminder from CBP
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is reminding travelers to declare meats, fruits, vegetables, and other agricultural items upon entry to the United States. Recent incidents of non-compliance have led to penalties for travelers. A TikToker faced a potential fine for forgetting to declare a banana, highlighting the importance of adhering to CBP regulations to avoid confiscation and fines.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What happened to UAE’s Iceberg Project? The ambitious plan to haul a colossal Antarctic iceberg to the coast of Fujairah
item.description: The UAE’s ambitious plan to tow a giant Antarctic iceberg for fresh water has stalled with no updates since its 2017 launch. Meanwhile, a Greenland startup successfully exports glacial ice to Dubai bars for luxury use. One aimed to solve a crisis; the other sells exclusivity. As of 2025, only cocktail glasses, not coastlines, are chilled.

item.title: Pope receives high-ranking Russian Orthodox cleric
item.description: Pope Leo XIV held a first meeting on Saturday with a senior Russian Orthodox cleric at the Vatican since becoming the head of the Catholic church earlier this year, the Holy See said without giving further details. The head of the Russian Orthodox Church, Patriarch Kirill, has sanctified Moscow's Ukraine invasion, which he has described as a "holy war."

item.title: 'My hand was hanging by a thread': Indian-origin man Saurabh Anand attacked by teen gang with a machete in Melbourne
item.description: Saurabh Anand, an Indian-origin man, was brutally attacked by a teen machete gang in Melbourne, resulting in severe injuries. The attack occurred at Central Square Shopping Centre in Altona Meadows, leaving Anand with a severed hand, head injuries, and broken bones. Doctors managed to reattach his hand after extensive surgery, while several teenagers were arrested in connection with the assault.

China PM warns against a global AI 'monopoly'
item.description: Premier Li Qiang announced China's plan to establish the World AI Cooperation Organization, aiming to foster international collaboration in AI development. This initiative seeks to prevent a technological monopoly by a few nations or companies, addressing concerns about job losses and economic disruption. Despite semiconductor shortages, China is committed to advancing its AI ambitions, spurred by the success of domestic AI ventures like DeepSeek.

item.title: Latest child to starve to death in Gaza weighed less than birth weight
No proof Hamas routinely stole UN aid: Israeli military officials
item.description: Despite Israel's claims that Hamas systematically stole UN aid to Gaza, senior Israeli military officials found no evidence to support this accusation. They acknowledged the UN's aid delivery system was largely effective. As Israel faces increased international pressure over humanitarian suffering, it has moved to replace the UN-led system with a private operation, resulting in a surge of Palestinian deaths due to gunfire while seeking aid.

item.title: Who is Gaza journalist Mohammed Abu Aoun who puts his camera, press shield on sale on LinkedIn for food?
item.description: A Gaza-based photojournalist is resorting to selling his equipment to feed his family amidst a looming famine. ​ "I am the photojournalistMohammed Abu Aoun from Gaza, I want to offer my equipment and the press shield for sale so that I can buy food for me and my family," his LinkedIn post read.

item.description: Kamala Harris made a brief return to the political stage via a pre-recorded video at a youth voters event in Washington, DC, urging young people to "stay in the fight." “Your generation has grown up on the front lines of so many crises — from COVID and the climate crisis to gun violence and mental health," Kamala Harris said.
